3 /// [The Blessed One said: "Furthermore, Mahāmati, there are four kinds of self-nature (svabhāva). What are the four? They are: the imagined self-nature (parikalpita-svabhāva), the dependent self-nature (paratantra-svabhāva), the perfected self-nature (pariniṣpanna-svabhāva), and the self-nature of the ultimate truth (paramārtha-svabhāva). /// [Mahāmati asked: "Blessed One, what is the characteristic of the imagined self-nature? [The Blessed One replied: "It is that which is grasped by the ignorant through names and signs (nāmanimitta) regarding objects that have no intrinsic nature. /// [Mahāmati asked: "Blessed One, what is the characteristic of the dependent self-nature? [The Blessed One replied: "It is the manifestation of the mind (cittadṛśya) appearing as various objects due to the habit-energy of false discrimination. /// [Mahāmati asked: "Blessed One, what is the characteristic of the perfected self-nature? [The Blessed One replied: "It is the state where the dependent self-nature is eternally free from the imagined self-nature. /// [Mahāmati asked: "Blessed One, what is the characteristic of the self-nature of the ultimate truth? [The Blessed One replied: "It is the realization of the non-arising of all phenomena (anutpāda-dharma) through the wisdom of the Tathāgatas. /// [Mahāmati asked: "Blessed One, why is it called 'self-nature'? [The Blessed One replied: "Because it is the essential nature of all dharmas, which is neither created nor destroyed, and is not subject to change; therefore, it is called 'self-nature'. /// [Mahāmati asked: "Blessed One, how many kinds of self-natures are there? [The Blessed One replied: "There are three kinds of self-natures: the self-nature of words (vāk-svabhāva), the self-nature of objects (artha-svabhāva), and the self-nature of reality (tattva-svabhāva). /// [Mahāmati asked: "Blessed One, what is the self-nature of words? [The Blessed One replied: "It is the conventional designation established by the power of linguistic habit. /// [Mahāmati asked: "Blessed One, what is the self-nature of objects? [The Blessed One replied: "It is the manifestation of the mind appearing as external objects. /// [Mahāmati asked: "Blessed One, what is the self-nature of reality? [The Blessed One replied: "It is the realm of the Tathāgatas, which is beyond the reach of words and thought, and is realized through the wisdom of non-discrimination. /// [Mahāmati asked: "Blessed One, how does one enter into the realization of these self-natures? [The Blessed One replied: "By abandoning the attachment to names and signs, and by realizing that all phenomena are like illusions and dreams, one enters into the realization of the self-natures. /// [Mahāmati asked: "Blessed One, for those who do not understand the self-natures, what faults arise? [The Blessed One replied: "They fall into the views of eternalism and nihilism, and they wander in the cycle of birth and death (saṃsāra) without attaining liberation. /// [Mahāmati asked: "Blessed One, how does one transcend the self-natures? [The Blessed One replied: "By cultivating the path of the Bodhisattvas, practicing the stages (bhūmi), and attaining the transformation of the basis (āśrayaparāvṛtti), one transcends the self-natures and realizes the stage of the Tathāgata. /// [Mahāmati asked: "Blessed One, what is the fruit of this realization? [The Blessed One replied: "The fruit is the attainment of the great compassion (mahākaruṇā) and the power to liberate all sentient beings, while remaining forever free from the defilements of the world. /// [Mahāmati asked: "Blessed One, how should one teach the Dharma to others regarding these self-natures? [The Blessed One replied: "One should teach according to the capacities of the listeners, using skillful means (upāya), and lead them gradually toward the realization of the true nature of reality. /// [Mahāmati asked: "Blessed One, is there any distinction between the self-natures of the Śrāvakas and the Bodhisattvas? [The Blessed One replied: "There is. The Śrāvakas realize the emptiness of the self but do not realize the emptiness of phenomena; the Bodhisattvas, however, realize both the emptiness of the self and the emptiness of phenomena. /// [Mahāmati asked: "Blessed One, what is the difference between the self-nature of the Śrāvakas and the self-nature of the Pratyekabuddhas? [The Blessed One replied: "The Śrāvakas focus on the cessation of suffering through the analysis of the aggregates, while the Pratyekabuddhas realize the dependent origination of phenomena and attain the wisdom of the twelve links of causation. /// [Mahāmati asked: "Blessed One, what is the self-nature of the Tathāgatas? [The Blessed One replied: "The self-nature of the Tathāgatas is the perfection of all virtues, the mastery of all dharmas, and the inexhaustible storehouse of the Dharma-realm (dharmadhātu). /// [Mahāmati asked: "Blessed One, how does one protect oneself from falling into the views of the outsiders (tīrthika) regarding these self-natures? [The Blessed One replied: "By understanding that all phenomena are devoid of intrinsic nature and are merely manifestations of the mind, one protects oneself from the views of the outsiders. /// [Mahāmati asked: "Blessed One, is there any dharma that exists apart from these self-natures? [The Blessed One replied: "No, Mahāmati. All dharmas are encompassed within these four self-natures. There is no dharma outside of them. /// [Mahāmati asked: "Blessed One, if all dharmas are encompassed within these self-natures, why do some people still cling to the notion of a permanent self (ātman)? [The Blessed One replied: "Because they have not yet severed the habit-energy of ignorance and have not realized the non-self (anātman) of persons and phenomena. /// [Mahāmati asked: "Blessed One, how can one sever the habit-energy of ignorance? [The Blessed One replied: "By practicing the meditation on the non-arising of all phenomena and by cultivating the wisdom of the Tathāgatas, one can sever the habit-energy of ignorance. /// [Mahāmati asked: "Blessed One, what is the final goal of these self-natures? [The Blessed One replied: "The final goal is the attainment of the Buddha-ground (buddhabhūmi), where all dualistic thoughts cease and the Dharma-body (dharmakāya) is fully realized. /// [Mahāmati asked: "Blessed One, how does one maintain the practice of these self-natures in daily life? [The Blessed One replied: "One should maintain the practice by being mindful of the emptiness of all things, by acting with compassion toward all sentient beings, and by never abandoning the vow to save them. /// [Mahāmati asked: "Blessed One, what are the benefits of understanding these self-natures? [The Blessed One replied: "One gains the power of eloquence, the ability to distinguish the true from the false, and the capacity to guide sentient beings to the path of liberation. /// [Mahāmati asked: "Blessed One, is there any danger in teaching these self-natures to those who are not yet prepared? [The Blessed One replied: "Yes, Mahāmati.
